results.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
results.proof_sketch: An induced-minor model gives these sets as the inverse images of the six target vertices under contractions. The absent target edge forces A and B to be anticomplete, since edge deletion is unavailable. Conversely, contract each connected set; all fourteen required edges appear and the A-B edge does not. For the algorithm, assign every vertex one of seven labels: unused or one of the six branch sets. For each assignment, test nonemptiness, connectivity, the forbidden A-B adjacency, and the fourteen required adjacencies. The labels themselves are a polynomial-size NP certificate.

results.claim: Bounded-skeleton structural reduction: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor if and only if it has six nonempty pairwise vertex-disjoint tree subgraphs TA,TB,T1,T2,T3,T4 and one selected cross-edge for each of the fourteen target edges, with no edge of G between TA and TB. The exceptional trees TA,TB may be chosen with at most four leaves and at most two vertices of tree-degree at least three; every core tree Ti may be chosen with at most five leaves and at most three vertices of tree-degree at least three. After suppressing unmarked degree-two vertices there are at most 44 essential vertices in total, and hence only finitely many marked skeleton types.
results.proof_sketch: Start with a branch model and select one actual cross-edge for each of the fourteen required target adjacencies. For target vertex v, let Xv be the set of endpoints of selected edges lying in its branch, so |Xv|≤d(v). In a spanning tree of that connected branch, take the minimal subtree containing Xv. Every leaf belongs to Xv, since any unmarked leaf could be deleted. For a nontrivial tree with ℓ leaves, Σdeg≥3(deg−2)=ℓ−2, so it has at most ℓ−2 vertices of degree at least three; the one-vertex case is immediate. Since d(A)=d(B)=4 and d(Ci)=5, the stated bounds follow. Restricting the branches to these subtrees preserves every selected cross-edge and preserves A-B anticompleteness. Conversely, the six tree vertex sets and fourteen selected edges satisfy the exact branch-set certificate, so contracting the trees gives K6 minus AB. Mark the selected-edge endpoints and suppress every unmarked degree-two vertex. Each branch then has at most d+(d−2)=2d−2 essential vertices: six for each exceptional tree and eight for each core tree, totaling 44. Thus only finitely many skeletons occur, although their edges may represent arbitrarily long paths.

results.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
results.proof_sketch: If q=0, G is complete and cannot contain two anticomplete nonempty branch sets. If q>0 and G has at least four universal vertices, the endpoints of any nonedge together with four universal vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise there are at most three universal vertices. Every remaining vertex is an endpoint of a nonedge, so there are at most 2q such vertices and n≤2q+3. Apply the seven-label algorithm from the first claim. This also gives a kernel: output a fixed yes/no instance in the two decided cases and retain G otherwise.

results.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
results.proof_sketch: Take a branch model and restrict G to its six branch sets. Each Ci supplies an A-B path whose internal vertices lie in Ci, so every separator disjoint from A∪B has size at least four. Choose an inclusion-minimal A-B separator S. Minimality makes each s∈S adjacent into both components DA and DB containing A and B. If two vertices of S were nonadjacent, shortest paths between them through DA and DB would form an induced cycle of length at least four; hence S is a clique. Each full component D contains a vertex complete to S: choose v∈D maximizing |N(v)∩S|. If s∈S misses v, take a shortest path v=p0,…,pk in D to a neighbor pk of s. For every t∈N(v)∩S, applying chordality to the cycle through t,p0,…,pk,s (using the last neighbor of t on the path) forces tpk to be an edge. Then pk has strictly more neighbors in S than v, a contradiction. Select S-complete vertices x∈DA and y∈DB and four vertices of S. Since x and y lie in different components, these six vertices induce precisely K6 minus xy.

results.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
results.proof_sketch: The two anticomplete exceptional branch sets must lie in one part: fixing a vertex in either set forces every vertex of the other set, and then of both sets, into that same part. Since a part is independent and each branch set is connected, both are singletons. A core branch touching them is either a singleton in another part or spans at least two parts. Any spanning branch can be shrunk to one cross-part edge; such an edge is adjacent to every other spanning branch and to every outside-part singleton. Singleton core branches must occupy distinct outside parts. Thus choose their part set J, and the remaining core branches are exactly disjoint cross-part edges, namely a matching. The displayed matching formula follows by pairing vertices from different parts: at most ⌊M/2⌋ edges are possible, and every edge uses a vertex outside a largest part, giving M−L; greedily pairing different largest remaining parts attains the minimum. Enumerating i,s,J costs O(r^5), after finding the parts as complement components.

results.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
results.proof_sketch: Use a nice tree decomposition. A state assigns each bag vertex one of the six branch labels or unused; records, for every label, the partition of its bag vertices into connected components already built; records whether that label is unseen, active, or completed; and stores fourteen bits for required inter-branch adjacencies. Processing an edge merges same-label components, sets the appropriate adjacency bit, or rejects an A-B edge. When the last bag vertex of a component is forgotten, separator locality implies that component cannot connect later, so it may disappear only as the unique component of its label, after which that label is closed. Join nodes combine partitions and adjacency bits. At the root require six nonempty connected labels and all fourteen bits. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a constant number of states, which is 2^{O(w log w)}.

results.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
results.proof_sketch: The two paths and the four singleton sets {ci} form a valid model. Suppose instead that an exceptional branch is {x}. Its four core neighbors require four distinct neighbors of x. Path vertices have degree at most three, so x=ci. The other exceptional branch Y is a connected interval in one component of A−ai or B−bi. Its four core neighbors require |N(Y)\Y|≥4. Up to swapping A,B and reversing indices, take x=c1 or c2. For c2, every allowable interval has at most three external neighbors. For c1, the only intervals with four external neighbors are {a2,a3} and {a2,a3,a4}. Their respective external neighborhoods are {a1,a4,c2,c3} and {a1,c2,c3,c4}. Four disjoint core branches must therefore use all four boundary vertices, including a1. But a1 is isolated after deleting x and Y, so its core branch is the singleton {a1}, anticomplete to the other three core branches—a contradiction. Symmetry handles all remaining cases.

results.claim: For every integer L≥1 there is a graph G_L on 6L+6 vertices that contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor, but in every model each of the two branch sets corresponding to the missing-edge endpoints has at least L+1 vertices. Hence no universal constant bounds either exceptional branch set in all models.
results.proof_sketch: Construct G_L from the preceding 12-vertex graph by replacing each edge of the two four-marked-vertex paths by a path of length L; retain the K4 on c1,c2,c3,c4 and the spokes from ci to the ith marked vertex of each path. The two whole paths and the four singleton ci form a model. Consider any model with exceptional branches X,Y and four core branches. The core-branch union is connected, lies in one component of G_L−(X∪Y), and contains four distinct neighbors of each of X and Y. Suppose X contains a designated clique vertex, and let I be the nonempty set of its designated clique vertices. Then Y contains no designated clique vertex, avoids the path marks indexed by I, and, being connected, is an interval of one subdivided path. Restore X except for those clique vertices. If a designated clique vertex remains, their common component sees Y through marked-vertex spokes and at most two path-boundary vertices. Every such boundary connection consumes an available marked index not already represented by a spoke, so this component has at most 4−|I|≤3 neighbors of Y; every other component has at most one. If none remains, all components have at most one neighbor of Y. Deleting the restored vertices cannot increase these numbers, contradicting the four core branches. Thus neither X nor Y meets the designated clique. Each is therefore a path interval. Its external neighborhood has at most two path-boundary vertices plus one ci per marked vertex it contains. Four distinct core neighbors force it to contain at least two marks, whose distance is at least L, so its size is at least L+1.

results.claim: Sharp obstruction at minimum width: for every L≥1, the graph G_L in the preceding claim has treewidth exactly 4 and order n=6L+6, while every model has each missing-edge endpoint branch set of size at least n/6. Hence even on treewidth-4 inputs—the minimum treewidth of any positive instance—no o(n) universal bound can be imposed on either exceptional branch set.
results.proof_sketch: The preceding claim gives order n=6L+6 and lower bound L+1=n/6. For the upper bound tw(G_L)≤4, eliminate the vertices of the first subdivided path in order from its first marked vertex toward its fourth, then do the same for the second path, and finally eliminate c1,c2,c3,c4. Along either path, fill edges propagate adjacency to the clique vertices whose marks have already been passed. An eliminated unmarked vertex has its successor and at most three such clique vertices as later neighbors; a marked vertex additionally sees its own ci, but before the fourth mark there are at most two earlier ci, and the fourth mark has no successor. Thus no elimination has more than four later neighbors. Conversely, contracting either whole path produces a K5 minor with c1,c2,c3,c4, so tw(G_L)≥4. This is the least possible width for a positive instance because K6 minus an edge contains K5 and every induced minor is a minor. At L=1, n=12 and the forced lower bound is 2, recovering the audited no-singleton boundary case.

final_writeup:
The unrestricted P-versus-NP-complete classification is not resolved here. The required structural lens gives an exact bounded-skeleton reformulation. Choose one witness edge for every target adjacency and replace each branch by a minimal subtree spanning its incident witness endpoints. The exceptional trees then have at most four leaves and two branching vertices, while each core tree has at most five leaves and three branching vertices. Suppressing unmarked degree-two vertices leaves at most 44 essential vertices, so only finitely many marked skeleton types occur. This transfers in both directions to the original branch-set certificate. It does not itself give a polynomial algorithm: skeleton edges may represent arbitrarily long paths, and the two exceptional trees must remain anticomplete.

The main positive structural result is that contractions give no additional power on chordal inputs: detection reduces to finding the six-vertex induced subgraph, yielding an elementary polynomial algorithm. Complete multipartite graphs admit a separate exact count-and-matching criterion, while arbitrary dense graphs have an FPT kernel in the number of missing edges. A standard connectivity dynamic program also handles supplied bounded-width decompositions.

The obstruction is stronger than merely requiring unbounded branch sets. The subdivided family has n=6L+6 vertices and forces each missing-edge endpoint branch to contain at least L+1=n/6 vertices in every model. It also has treewidth exactly 4: path-order elimination gives width at most four, while contraction gives a K5 minor. Since every positive instance has treewidth at least four, this occurs at the minimum possible width. Thus enumeration restricted to singleton exceptional branches, to a fixed size cap, or even to any sublinear size cap is not a complete strategy, including on treewidth-4 inputs. These partial results isolate tractable regimes and establish a precise linear normalization obstruction, but they supply neither an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm nor an unrestricted hardness result.
